name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,421

clue.text: Royal Institution getting bass and musicians award for achievement

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the Royal Institution
B is the musical abbreviation for bass
a group of musicians playing together

explanation.surface: A scientific society honours a bass player and his group with a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribband is an older spelling of ribbon, the coloured strip worn as a decoration or medal for distinguished service.

clue.text: Father tucked into remnants of meal

indicators.note: something tucked into another is pushed inside it

blocks.note: the rest is what remains
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad tucks into the leftovers of dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Tucked into sounds like eating heartily, but it is the signal to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal, the food eaten at one sitting.

clue.text: Fixed bayonets at port leading to political protest

indicators.note: something fixed has been rigged or rearranged, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: Soldiers with bayonets fixed at a harbour spark a political demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: Fixed bayonets is the military order, so 'Fixed' reads as part of the picture rather than the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boston Tea Party of 1773 was a colonial protest against British taxation, when tea was dumped into the harbour.

clue.text: Teenager makes smell after beer-drinking party

indicators.note: drinking something takes it inside, so the beer holds the next piece
after places one piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
a do is an informal word for a party
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A teenager whiffs after a boozy party.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person in the years between childhood and adulthood, roughly the teenage years.

clue.text: Determination to jump into river? On the contrary

indicators.note: into places one piece inside another
this flips the instruction just given, so the outer and inner pieces swap roles

blocks.note: to dive is to jump headfirst
standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A swimmer resolves to leap into a river, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: As written, the jump goes into the river; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so R goes inside DIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is energy and ambition, the motivation or determination to achieve something.

clue.text: Police force welcoming popular copper's attitude

indicators.note: a host welcoming guests takes them inside, so the force wraps round what follows

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
in fashion, popular
a copper is a penny, abbreviated d in old British money, with the 's read as S

explanation.surface: The police welcome a well-liked officer and his outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman in this police-force surface, but it is the coin: d stood for a penny in pre-decimal British currency, and the apostrophe-s supplies a letter too.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a fixed way of thinking, the mental outlook or disposition someone brings to things.

clue.text: Babe finally tucked up in manger rocked by extremely impressive collection of animals

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, keeping only its closing letter
rocked means shaken about, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
extremely means at the extremes, keeping only the outermost letters

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: The baby Jesus lies tucked up in a rocking manger, surrounded by an impressive array of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild or exotic animals kept for display.

clue.text: Article about a new type of bread

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the article is read backwards

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
taken as written
standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A news piece about a novel kind of loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a leavened flatbread from South Asian cooking, baked in a tandoor oven.

clue.text: Eatery in university implicated in outbreak of rash and Irritable Bowel Syndrome

indicators.note: something implicated in an affair is caught up inside it
an outbreak scatters things wildly, so the letters break out into new order

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for university
taken as written
the usual initials for the condition

explanation.surface: A campus restaurant is blamed for an outbreak of rashes and stomach trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sushi bar is a restaurant serving Japanese raw fish and rice dishes, a kind of eatery.

clue.text: See 2
Cooking pots contain dregs of Bolognese sauce

indicators.note: dregs are what is left at the bottom, so only the final letter of the word is kept
cooking cooks up something new, so these letters are reworked into another order
the rearranged letters hold the other piece inside them

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pans on the stove still hold the last of a spaghetti sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged pot letters give PSTO, and the E sits inside after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil, pine-nut and garlic paste served on pasta.

clue.text: One working with Asian swimming across eastern part of Mediterranean

indicators.note: letters swimming about are thrown out of order and must be rearranged
lying across something means stretching around it, so the jumbled letters enclose a piece

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
on, as a machine is when running
taken as written
standard abbreviation for east or eastern

explanation.surface: Someone and an Asian companion swim across a stretch of the Med.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionian Sea is the arm of the Mediterranean lying between southern Italy and western Greece.

clue.text: Cook goes with net to catch chicken in ancient monument

indicators.note: to cook something up is to concoct it, so the letters are reworked into a new order
catching something means holding it, so the reworked letters surround a piece

blocks.note: the letters of both words, joined by 'with'
a hen is a female chicken

explanation.surface: A cook takes a net to trap a chicken at an old historic site.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain in England, a famous ancient monument.

clue.text: Permit 6 to visit South Africa

indicators.note: one piece pays a call on the next, so the two are set side by side

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for six
standard abbreviation for South Africa

explanation.surface: Six people need a document to travel to South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 is a number, not a cross-reference to the clue at 6.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement in a passport that permits the holder to enter a country.

clue.text: By which to find out what went wrong with parking at most hectic northbound subway?

definitions.text: By which to find out what went wrong

indicators.note: hectic means frantic and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
in a down entry, heading north means travelling upwards, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
taken as written
a metro is an underground railway

explanation.surface: An inquiry into what went wrong with the parking at the busiest northbound station.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening phrase, describing what the answer is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem is an examination after a death, or figuratively any analysis after failure, to establish causes.

clue.text: Medium crayon vital for editing?

indicators.note: text up for editing will be cut and rearranged, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: An art supply of middling size is essential when correcting work.
explanation.walkthrough: Medium looks like a size of crayon; it is the spiritualist.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium is a person claiming to contact spirits, and a clairvoyant claims to see beyond normal senses.

clue.text: Get-up worn by little child meeting Latin philosopher

indicators.note: clothing worn by someone goes around them, so the outfit encloses the following pieces

blocks.note: to get up is to arise
a tot is a small child
standard abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A toddler in fancy dress meets a Roman thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Get-up reads as an outfit, which is why 'worn by' fits the surface; in the wordplay it is the verb to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato and tutor to Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Complaints made by side beaten crossing oceans

indicators.note: beaten means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
crossing something means spanning it, so the reworked letters stretch around it

blocks.note: taken as written
seas are oceans

explanation.surface: A defeated team grumbles about a long sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaints suggests grumbling, but here it means illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment or illness, so diseases are complaints.

clue.text: Soprano caught top of nail in make-up sponge

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its opening letter
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for soprano
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
rouge is a red cosmetic
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A singer is caught catching her nail on a cosmetic sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: Make-up sponge looks like one phrase, but sponge alone is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others, cadging money or food, which is exactly what scrounging means.

clue.text: Clutching money, innocent abroad is lacking in self restraint

indicators.note: clutching means holding tight, so the reworked letters grip a piece inside
abroad suggests going far and wide, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A naive traveller abroad, hanging on to his cash, cannot control himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Incontinent describes someone unable to restrain their appetites or bodily functions, a lack of self-control.

clue.text: Publisher passionate about language

indicators.note: the answer is found about, that is within, the run of letters

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A publisher is enthusiastic about language.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpa is the Tibetan-related language spoken by the Sherpa people of Nepal's Himalayan region.

clue.text: Underwear worn by Her Majesty's composer

indicators.note: in a down entry, a garment worn by someone sits on top of them, so one piece comes first

blocks.note: a bra is an item of underwear
HM abbreviates Her Majesty, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: The Queen's composer wears her lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was the nineteenth-century German Romantic composer of symphonies and the German Requiem.

clue.text: God makes mistakes over replacing king

indicators.note: one letter replacing another takes its place, swapping one for the other

blocks.note: to err is to make a mistake
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A deity slips up when standing in for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: O takes the place of one R in ERRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Son gets awfully hot temper from family member, ...

indicators.note: done awfully, the words are badly mangled and come out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for son
the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A boy suffers a fierce outburst from a relative, the trailing dots carrying the story on.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepmother is a father's later wife, a relation by marriage and so a member of the household.

clue.text: Latin American ditching his alarm ...

indicators.note: ditching something means throwing it away, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: Hispanic describes Spanish-speaking Latin Americans
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Latin American man throws away his alarm clock, the dots carrying the tale on.
explanation.walkthrough: His looks like a possessive tied to alarm, but it is the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, the same sense as alarm when used as a noun.

clue.text: ... in place of endless idleness

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: sloth is laziness

explanation.surface: The sentence continues: panic in place of endless laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is a position or space allotted to someone, such as a slot in a schedule.

clue.text: ... one sitting round fire close to tent is one of a kind

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the closing letter is kept
sitting round something means encircling it, so the outer piece goes around the rest

blocks.note: a loose reading: ON as in sitting on, with S
an ingle is a fire on a hearth, as in inglenook
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone sits by a campfire outside a tent, a solitary figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's 'one sitting' for the outer letters is loose: ON is the familiar 'sitting' (sitting on), with S. An ingle is an old Scots word for a hearth fire, as in inglenook.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a single thing standing alone, something unique rather than one of a set or pair.

clue.text: Light seen in Kent orchard

indicators.note: something seen in a phrase is visible within its run of letters

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A glow is spotted among the fruit trees in Kent, England's garden county.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable lamp, a source of light carried in the hand.

clue.text: Saint Peter prepared to carry the top of Christ's ceremonial staff

indicators.note: prepared means made up or worked over, so the name is reworked into new order
the top of a word in a down-style reading is its opening letter only

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for saint
taken as written
the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: The apostle Peter readies himself to bear the head of Jesus's sacred rod.
explanation.walkthrough: The C is carried along inside the reworked letters of PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the ornamental rod carried by a monarch on ceremonial occasions as a symbol of sovereignty.

clue.text: Instrument made by halfwit attending secondary school

blocks.note: comp is British slang for a comprehensive, a state secondary school
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An instrument is built by a dim pupil at a secondary school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attending' places the fool alongside the school, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass is a navigational instrument with a magnetised needle, or a drawing tool for circles.
